title: Stop trying to “focus”—ADHD isn’t a sniper rifle
summary:
The most quotable take came from @visakanv: “how do I focus with adhd” is the wrong question—“it’s like asking ‘how do I use a Gatling gun like a sniper rifle.’” His whole arc is basically: ADHD isn’t a moral failure, it’s a different machine, and you should build external infrastructure (notes, threads, logs) instead of trying to shame yourself into acting neurotypical.

This strand starts way back in 2018 with Visa admitting he “taught myself to manage my ADHD with notes and threads,” calling it a “prosthetic” he stopped being ashamed of and started treating like “a mecha for the mind.” The “core practice” that keeps resurfacing is his distraction-log move: when you procrastinate, take meticulous notes anyway—turn “watching trashy movies” into “deep-self-directed work.” The trigger moment that turns this into a community artifact is 2021’s “are you also a fidgety boi?” tweet launching the Constructive ADHD Google Doc, which becomes the thing everyone keeps linking for years. Peaks include the 2022 viral reframe “ADHD is really ODD—Obedience Deficit Disorder” (some of us are wired to disobey), and the 2023 escalation where he basically declares distractions economically rational: “all my most valuable ideas started as distractions,” valuing his “distracted life” at ~$30m vs $4m for the “focused life.” Along the way he adds a gentler pedagogy beat (the “Dinesh” anecdote: replace punishment/contrition with curiosity and causal debugging), and a later somatic twist: the “chaos mind problem” isn’t solved in the mind but “in the body, since that’s where the feelings are.”

What dies off is any pretense of one-size-fits-all productivity discipline—Visa repeatedly rejects rigid routines (“weekly review” made him feel drained), and reframes the whole conversation as designing a life that fits your brain. The payoff is real-world validation: therapists like @univrsw3th4rt want to use it with clients, and in 2024 @QiaochuYuan’s ADHD megathread puts Visa’s doc at #1 as “actionable advice,” basically canonizing it. If you’ve ever felt broken because you can’t “just do the thing,” this thread is the opposite of motivational scolding: it’s a blueprint for turning chaos into a system—and maybe even an edge.
